Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.

You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule: TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return

Preferred position:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.


Fallback position:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

Drafter's locked target level: preferred

Original clause:
10. EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION
10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.

Rendered redlined clause:
10. EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION
10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
10.3 Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of expiry or termination, return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.

Customer Data: 1.3 “Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.
Deliverable: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

[{"id":"f-lol-cap-7df8de07","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","rationale":"Section 21 meets the preferred position in full. The cap in 21.1 is expressly mutual and set at the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event and USD 1,000,000; \"Fees\" (1.5) means recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the cap base is meaningful and not illusory. 21.2 is a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and, favourably to us, preserves data restoration, replacement services, notice and incident response costs as direct damages. 21.3 carves out (uncapped) breach of confidentiality, data-protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP, and confirms Customer's payment of undisputed Fees is not \"damages\" subject to the cap. 21.4 preserves independence of each cap and survival on failure of essential purpose. No competing or one-sided liability language appears elsewhere (18.1 is insurance only, with cyber cover of USD 5,000,000 sitting above the cap). No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-f67decf2","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","rationale":"Section 24 matches our preferred position: 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free affiliate/successor (M&A) assignment right on prompt notice; 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment, delegation and transfer by change of control to Customer's consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor; 24.3 applies a reasonable-consent standard to other assignments; and 24.4 confirms Customer's change of control gives Vendor no right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees or reduce service. Section 13.3 aligns licence transfer with permitted Section 24 assignments, and no other provision creates a change-of-control exit or re-pricing right for Vendor (9.2 is a standard insolvency clause that expressly excludes lawful reorganizations). No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-260158b0","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer; § 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to engage any supplier and disclaims any exclusivity commitment, which meets the preferred position. A full-text search for exclusivity language returned only exclusivity that runs in our favour or is unrelated (non-exclusive licence grant in § 13.1, IP ownership, exclusive remedy/jurisdiction wording). The § 7.2 disclose-and-match right and the § 2.1 take-or-pay minimum operate as commercial friction rather than an exclusive-dealing covenant, and are addressed under the MFN and minimum-commitment rules — we do not double-flag them here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-4812bbcd","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 27.3 If a force-majeure event materially prevents an affected Service for more than fifteen consecutive days, Customer may procure substitute services and suspend affected Fees. After thirty consecutive days, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination fee payable by Customer: searches for \"liquidated damages\", \"penalty\", \"termination fee\" and Customer payment obligations return nothing of that kind. Sections 9 and 10 give termination rights without any exit charge, § 27.3 expressly allows force-majeure termination \"without penalty\", § 7.1 bars unstated minimum-use or similar charges, and § 21.3 confirms Customer's only payment duty is undisputed Fees for conforming Services. This meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages). The § 2.1 take-or-pay commitment is an economic exposure but is a minimum-commitment term addressed under MINCOMMIT, not a liquidated damages or penalty clause, so it is not flagged here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-f190ec3e","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. The failure is Section 14.2: Vendor takes exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for Customer (per the § 1.4 definition), and the only licence back is revocable, non-transferable and limited to the Order Form term. That misses the preferred position (Customer ownership by assignment) and also fails the fallback, which requires a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables. Section 13.2's perpetual licence does not cure this because it covers only Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, not the Deliverable itself. Redline flips the assignment to Customer while expressly preserving Vendor Technology under 14.3; the licence-back fallback is offered in the comment.","proposal":"Add a fallback clause: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer gets a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-license-06449018","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.","rationale":"The core Services and paid-up licence grants are strong: § 13.1 (p0048) extends access to Customer, its Affiliates and contractors; § 13.2 (p0049) gives a perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid licence to delivered/embedded Vendor Technology for Customer and its Affiliates; and § 13.3 (p0050) permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor and limits revocation/suspension to uncured material breach after notice and cure. Those meet the preferred position. The Deliverable licence in § 14.2 (p0054), however, is expressly \"revocable, non-transferable\" and expires with the Order Form term, with no path to cover Affiliates or contractors — a revocable-at-Vendor's-discretion grant that sits in walk-away territory and conflicts with §§ 13.3 and 10.1. Deliverable ownership itself is left to the IP rule; this finding addresses only the licence scope. Redline makes the Deliverable licence perpetual and irrevocable, extends it to Affiliates and contractors, and permits successor transfer via § 13.3.","proposal":"Make the Deliverable licence perpetual and irrevocable, and add one sentence covering Affiliates, contractors, and successor transfer.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-mfn-aa0c1dbb","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.","rationale":"The MFN here runs the wrong way: it binds us (Customer), not Vendor. It is open-ended — every \"more favourable commercial offer\" we receive, with no product limitation, no time limit, and no reasonable-comparison carve-outs — so it fails the fallback (MFN limited to a defined product, 12 months, with carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory. It also requires disclosure of third-party pricing, which raises confidentiality and antitrust exposure, and it directly contradicts § 12.3 (p0044), where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. Redline deletes the obligation; any Vendor-granted MFN in our favour would remain acceptable.","proposal":"Negate the customer-side disclose-and-match MFN obligation in § 7.2.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-mincommit-953097f3","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay on Customer for three years expressly \"without reduction or termination rights\" — precisely the walk-away position under this rule, and well short of the fallback (a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, trued up rather than penalised). Nothing elsewhere provides an exit: Section 8.1 fixes a three-year term and Section 9 gives only cause-based termination rights, with no convenience termination or commitment reduction. It also directly conflicts with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. We proposed the preferred position (no minimum commitment; pay for Services ordered and used), which is consistent with §§ 7.1 and 12.3, and flagged the 12-month reducible commitment with true-up as a fallback in the comment.","proposal":"Remove the three-year take-or-pay commitment; fees payable for Services ordered/used only","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-noncompete-00a4a55e","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.","rationale":"§ 12.4 binds the Customer (us) with a post-term non-compete of twenty-four months covering any competing product or service in any territory, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (indeed acquisitions are expressly captured). That is walk-away territory under the rule: post-term duration exceeds 12 months and the scope is undefined/unlimited, so it fails the fallback (single named product, term only, ≤12 months, with carve-outs). It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. We propose deleting § 12.4 to reach the preferred position, and can offer the narrowed fallback if the Vendor shows a genuine need.","proposal":"Turn § 12.4's non-compete operator from \"shall not\" to \"may\" so no competing-product or territory restriction binds Customer.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-30553066","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.","rationale":"§ 12.4 binds only the Customer and is walk-away territory under the rule: it is an express no-hire (\"hire, or employ\"), it covers every Vendor employee rather than only personnel involved in the Services, it runs 24 months, and the phrase \"regardless of how the employee applies\" deliberately eliminates any general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. It therefore fails the fallback (mutual, involvement-limited, 12 months, carve-outs, no no-hire) on every material term. It also conflicts with § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no no-hire commitment and may hire anyone responding to general recruitment. Redline deletes the clause to reach the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), with the mutual 12-month fallback offered in the comment.","proposal":"Delete the one-sided 24-month no-hire imposed on Customer (§ 12.4)","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-t4c-e4e5ac6f","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.","rationale":"Section 9 contains only cause-based exits (9.1 material breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 security/SLA/legal failures) plus force majeure in 27.3; there is no Customer termination-for-convenience right anywhere (no 9.4 exists), and Section 2.1 affirmatively strips termination rights across a three-year take-or-pay commitment (Section 8.1 term is three years). That is walk-away territory under the rule: no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term. Vendor has no convenience right, which is consistent with the preferred position and is preserved. We inserted a new Section 9.4 at the preferred position (30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience right) and conformed Section 2.1 so the take-or-pay language does not nullify it; the fallback (60 days plus a fee capped at three months' Fees) is offered in the comment.","proposal":"Insert Section 9.4 giving Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no Vendor convenience right during a committed term.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-transition-5851bad4","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.","rationale":"Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) covers only access cut-off after an undefined \"agreed transition period\" (10.1) and Deliverable delivery/refunds (10.2). Section 16.5 expressly carves Customer Data out of the confidentiality return/destroy mechanic and defers it to \"Sections 11 and 15\" — Section 11 does not exist in the document and Section 15 contains no return, export, or deletion mechanics. This is a hosted-services agreement, so the absence fails even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export). Proposed insertion of a new 10.3 at the preferred position: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, and certified deletion thereafter.","proposal":"Insert new 10.3 requiring transition assistance, 30-day data return and certified deletion.","verification":"repaired"}]

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel, Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook and confirmed **19 findings**: 9 compliant, 7 deviations and 3 rules with no usable clause in the document.

The good news is that the provisions that usually consume the most negotiating time are already at our preferred position and need no redline. The liability cap (§ 21) is mutual, set at the greater of twelve months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. Assignment and change of control (§ 24), the audit right (§ 22), auto-renewal and uplift (§ 8), the performance warranty (§ 19) and Vendor insurance (§ 18, including USD 5,000,000 cyber cover) all meet the preferred position, and the Agreement imposes no liquidated damages or penalty on us.

The problems are concentrated in three places. First, a cluster of one-sided restrictions on **us** — a three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights (§ 2.1), a customer-side disclose-and-match MFN (§ 7.2), a 24-month non-compete and a 24-month no-hire (§ 12.4) — each of which sits in walk-away territory and each of which directly contradicts Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3 that we have made no such commitments. Second, **structural gaps**: there is no indemnification clause anywhere (the Section 20 cross-referenced in § 9.3 does not exist), no Customer termination for convenience, and no exit/transition, data-return or deletion mechanic despite this being a hosted-services deal handling our health data. Third, **Deliverables**: § 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of everything built for us with only a revocable, term-limited licence back, failing both the preferred position and the fallback.

The document is also internally inconsistent in ways that need fixing regardless of commercial outcome: § 28.1 (Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction) conflicts with § 28.2 (exclusive New York County jurisdiction); § 16.5 defers Customer Data return to "Sections 11 and 15" when Section 11 does not exist and Section 15 contains no such mechanics; and Section 23 is a bare heading.

Our proposed redlines are drafted and verified for most items. Three — governing law (§ 28.1), the minimum commitment (§ 2.1) and the no-hire (§ 12.4) — could not be cleanly effected in the markup and require manual drafting and direct negotiation.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; full uncapped carve-outs. No redline. |
| 2 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 | Consent-free affiliate/successor assignment for us; Vendor assignment restricted; no CoC exit or repricing. |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No exclusivity on us; § 12.3 affirmatively preserves our supplier freedom. |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 27.3 | No LDs, penalties or exit fees; force-majeure termination expressly "without penalty". |
| 5 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, independent auditor, Vendor-borne costs. |
| 6 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 8.2 | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension; uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| 7 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 | Professional/workmanlike, conformity to documentation; Hosted Services warranted for full term; mutual disclaimer does not swallow warranties. |
| 8 | Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — outside the accepted list and in conflict with § 28.2 (New York County). Redline not yet effected. |
| 9 | Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | (no Section 20; § 19.5 nearest) | No indemnity of any kind; § 9.3 cross-refers to a non-existent Section 20.5. New Section 20 inserted. |
| 10 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber/privacy 5M, term plus one year; insurance expressly does not cap liability. |
| 11 | Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 14.2 | Vendor owns all Deliverables; licence back revocable and term-limited. Fails preferred and fallback. Redline inserted. |
| 12 | Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 14.2 | Deliverable licence revocable, non-transferable, expires with the Order Form; conflicts with §§ 13.3 and 10.1. Redline inserted. |
| 13 | Low | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | Open-ended customer-side disclose-and-match; no product, time or comparison limits; contradicts § 12.3. Redline inserted. |
| 14 | Low | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | § 2.1 | USD 2,000,000 per year for three years, take-or-pay, expressly without reduction or termination rights. Redline not yet effected. |
| 15 | Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | 24 months post-term, any competing product, any territory, acquisitions captured; contradicts § 12.3. Redline inserted. |
| 16 | Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | One-sided 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees, general-advertising carve-out expressly removed. Redline not yet effected. |
| 17 | Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9.3 (cause-based only) | No Customer convenience right in a three-year term; § 2.1 strips termination rights. New § 9.4 inserted. |
| 18 | Low | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 10.2 | No exit assistance, data export or certified deletion; § 16.5 defers to a non-existent Section 11. New § 10.3 inserted. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook. We should not sign the Agreement in its current form until each is resolved.

1. **§ 2.1 — three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights (MINCOMMIT).** The express removal of reduction and termination rights is the walk-away position; nothing elsewhere provides an exit, as § 8.1 fixes a three-year term and Section 9 is cause-based only. Preferred: no minimum commitment, pay for Services ordered and used. Fallback: a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, trued up rather than penalised.
2. **No indemnification clause (INDEMN).** No Vendor IP indemnity at all, and the missing Section 20 leaves § 9.3, § 21.3, § 29.2 and § 30.5 with broken cross-references. We have inserted a Section 20 at the preferred position, with our own indemnity kept narrow to Customer-provided content and our breach of law.
3. **No Customer termination for convenience (T4C).** No convenience right anywhere in a multi-year committed term. We have inserted § 9.4 (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience right) and conformed § 2.1. Fallback: 60 days plus a fee capped at three months' Fees.
4. **§ 7.2 — customer-side disclose-and-match MFN.** Unlimited as to product, time and comparison, and it requires us to disclose third-party pricing, raising confidentiality and antitrust exposure. It contradicts § 12.3. Deletion sought; a Vendor-granted MFN in our favour would remain acceptable.
5. **§ 12.4 — 24-month post-term non-compete (NONCOMPETE).** Any competing product or service, any territory, no internal-development carve-out and acquisitions expressly captured. Contradicts § 12.3. Deletion sought; the narrowed fallback (single named product, term only, ≤12 months, with carve-outs) is available if Vendor shows genuine need.
6. **§ 12.4 — 24-month no-hire (NOSOLICIT).** One-sided, covers every Vendor employee rather than personnel involved in the Services, and "regardless of how the employee applies" deliberately eliminates the general-advertising carve-out. Deletion sought; fallback is mutual, involvement-limited, 12 months, with carve-outs and no no-hire.
7. **§ 14.2 — revocable, term-limited Deliverable licence (LICENSE).** A grant revocable at Vendor's discretion is walk-away territory and conflicts with §§ 13.3 and 10.1. We seek a perpetual, irrevocable grant extending to Affiliates and contractors, transferable under § 13.3.
8. **§ 28.1 — Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction (GOVLAW).** Outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and effectively an exclusive foreign venue, in direct conflict with § 28.2.

**Adjacent to walk-away:** § 14.2 Deliverable ownership (IP) fails both preferred and fallback, and the absence of any transition, data-return and deletion mechanic (TRANSITION) fails even the fallback in a hosted-services deal involving our health data.

---

## 4. Next steps

# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel, Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook and confirmed **19 findings**: 9 compliant, 7 deviations and 3 rules with no usable clause in the document.

The good news is that the provisions that usually consume the most negotiating time are already at our preferred position and need no redline. The liability cap (§ 21) is mutual, set at the greater of twelve months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. Assignment and change of control (§ 24), the audit right (§ 22), auto-renewal and uplift (§ 8), the performance warranty (§ 19) and Vendor insurance (§ 18, including USD 5,000,000 cyber cover) all meet the preferred position, and the Agreement imposes no liquidated damages or penalty on us.

The problems are concentrated in three places. First, a cluster of one-sided restrictions on **us** — a three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights (§ 2.1), a customer-side disclose-and-match MFN (§ 7.2), a 24-month non-compete and a 24-month no-hire (§ 12.4) — each of which sits in walk-away territory and each of which directly contradicts Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3 that we have made no such commitments. Second, **structural gaps**: there is no indemnification clause anywhere (the Section 20 cross-referenced in § 9.3 does not exist), no Customer termination for convenience, and no exit/transition, data-return or deletion mechanic despite this being a hosted-services deal handling our health data. Third, **Deliverables**: § 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of everything built for us with only a revocable, term-limited licence back, failing both the preferred position and the fallback.

The document is also internally inconsistent in ways that need fixing regardless of commercial outcome: § 28.1 (Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction) conflicts with § 28.2 (exclusive New York County jurisdiction); § 16.5 defers Customer Data return to "Sections 11 and 15" when Section 11 does not exist and Section 15 contains no such mechanics; and Section 23 is a bare heading.

Our proposed redlines are drafted and verified for most items. Three — governing law (§ 28.1), the minimum commitment (§ 2.1) and the no-hire (§ 12.4) — could not be cleanly effected in the markup and require manual drafting and direct negotiation.
